# RunVouch

> RunVouch is the watchdog for unattended AI agents, with a tamper-evident proof per run: a dead man's switch, cost cap and outcome check for Claude Code Routines, headless `claude -p`, OpenClaw, n8n and cron'd LLM scripts. It alerts within minutes when a scheduled agent is MISSED, FAILED, reported success without evidence (NO_EVIDENCE), stuck in a RETRY_STORM, over BUDGET, DRIFTing, or STALLED. Alerts via e-mail, Telegram, Slack or webhook; PagerDuty on Team. History 7 days on Free, 90 days on Solo and Team. Free for 3 agents; $9 Solo; $29 Team. Self-hostable (MIT).

Install: `pip install runvouch` (or `curl -fsSL https://runvouch.com/rv -o ~/bin/rv && chmod +x ~/bin/rv`) then `rv agent NAME --cadence 24h --evidence` and `rv run NAME --evidence-file OUT -- your-command`.
Claude Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add runvouch/claude-plugin` → `/plugin install runvouch`.
Claude Desktop bundle: https://runvouch.com/runvouch.mcpb
Remote MCP (official registry, com.runvouch/runvouch): `claude mcp add --transport http runvouch https://api.runvouch.com/mcp --header "X-API-Key: rv_…"`.
API base: https://api.runvouch.com (header X-API-Key).

## Docs
- [Claude Code](https://runvouch.com/docs/claude-code): Routines, headless runs, hooks plugin, transcript cost
- [Cron & scripts](https://runvouch.com/docs/cron): rv run for any job; GitHub Actions
- [Python & Node](https://runvouch.com/docs/python-node): LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI callbacks
- [Agent templates](https://runvouch.com/docs/templates): three copy-paste agents on official SEC and career-site data (DataSignals Lab), wrapped in rv run with evidence and cost caps
- [Verifiable agent runs](https://runvouch.com/verifiable-agent-runs): who needs a tamper-evident record of what an AI agent did (finance, compliance, EU AI Act logging and record-keeping duties, audits), what is and is not in the record, and how to verify it without trusting RunVouch
- [Verifiable runs](https://runvouch.com/docs/proof): every finished run gets a sha256 leaf, every UTC day a Merkle root chained to the previous day and stamped with OpenTimestamps (Bitcoin); public day files at https://api.runvouch.com/proof/, offline verifier script
- [Alert channels](https://runvouch.com/docs/alerts): e-mail, Telegram, Slack incoming webhook and JSON webhook on every plan; PagerDuty Events API v2 on Team (incident per agent and kind, resolved on ack); Solo and Team deliver MISSED and FAILED without the 10-minute cooldown
- [GitHub Actions](https://runvouch.com/docs/github-actions) · [OpenClaw](https://runvouch.com/docs/openclaw) · [n8n](https://runvouch.com/docs/n8n) · [MCP server](https://runvouch.com/docs/mcp) · [HTTP API](https://runvouch.com/docs/api)

## Field notes (blog)
- [My Claude Code cron ran up $1,800 in two nights. The watchdog that stops it at $2](https://runvouch.com/blog/claude-code-cron-unexpected-api-bill-runaway-cost-overnight): Four documented runaway agent bills ($1,818, $6,000, $437, $150), why per-call metrics hide the loop, and per-run/per-day caps with rv.
- [Claude Code Routine failed silently? How to know your scheduled agent actually ran](https://runvouch.com/blog/claude-code-routine-failed-silently-scheduled-task-didnt-run): Green does not mean done. The 4 ways a scheduled Claude Code run fails with no error, and heartbeat plus evidence checks that catch each one.
- [The dead man's switch for AI agents (and why a ping isn't enough)](https://runvouch.com/blog/dead-mans-switch-for-ai-agents): A ping monitor knows a job ran. For an agent that is the least interesting fact. What a dead man's switch has to check when the job is an LLM.
- [OpenClaw stuck in a polling loop: $150, a crash, and no alert. Detect it in 60 seconds](https://runvouch.com/blog/openclaw-stuck-in-polling-loop-150-no-alert): An OpenClaw agent called the same tool 1,535 times in two hours. Every call looked fine. How a retry-storm rule and a daily cap catch this before the bill.
- [7 ways unattended AI agents fail silently, and one check for each](https://runvouch.com/blog/7-ways-unattended-ai-agents-fail-silently): Seven ways a scheduled AI agent fails without an error, from a run that never starts to a run that does nothing, and the one detector that catches each.
- [Prove what your AI agent did: an audit trail for unattended agents](https://runvouch.com/blog/prove-what-your-ai-agent-did-audit-trail-for-unattended-agents): A real, tamper-evident proof of one agent run: hashed record, public daily Merkle chain, Bitcoin anchor. How to verify it with a stdlib script, and what it cannot prove.

## Integrations (one page per runtime: where the job runs, key as secret, snippet, what fails silently there)
- [Kubernetes CronJob](https://runvouch.com/integrations/kubernetes-cronjob): Alert when a Kubernetes CronJob stops firing, exits 0 without doing the work, loops, or an LLM job inside it overspends. One line in the container command.
- [systemd timers](https://runvouch.com/integrations/systemd-timers): Get alerted when a systemd timer stops firing or its service fails silently, including user timers. Wrap ExecStart with rv run.
- [GitLab CI scheduled pipelines](https://runvouch.com/integrations/gitlab-ci-schedules): Catch GitLab pipeline schedules that stop running (owner token expired, schedule deactivated) or pass without producing the artifact. One job line.
- [Jenkins](https://runvouch.com/integrations/jenkins): Alert when a Jenkins job with a cron trigger stops running or passes without its artifact, without touching Jenkins notifications.
- [Heroku Scheduler](https://runvouch.com/integrations/heroku-scheduler): Heroku Scheduler is documented as best effort and can skip runs. RunVouch alerts when a scheduled dyno did not start or its task did nothing.
- [AWS Lambda + EventBridge Scheduler](https://runvouch.com/integrations/aws-lambda-eventbridge): Alert when an EventBridge schedule stops invoking your Lambda, the function returns early without doing the work, or an LLM call inside it overspends.
- [Google Cloud Scheduler](https://runvouch.com/integrations/google-cloud-scheduler): Alert when a Cloud Scheduler job stops firing, the Cloud Run job or function returns 2xx without doing the work, or an LLM step overspends.
- [Azure Functions timer trigger](https://runvouch.com/integrations/azure-functions-timer): Alert when an Azure Functions timer trigger stops running (app stopped, scale-to-zero on Consumption) or completes without doing the work.
- [Cloudflare Workers Cron Triggers](https://runvouch.com/integrations/cloudflare-workers-cron): Two fetch() calls in your scheduled() handler give a Cloudflare Worker cron a dead man's switch, evidence and a cost cap.
- [Vercel Cron Jobs](https://runvouch.com/integrations/vercel-cron): Vercel cron calls a route and records the status code. RunVouch adds the missing part: did the route do the work, on time, within budget.
- [Supabase (pg_cron + Edge Functions)](https://runvouch.com/integrations/supabase-pg-cron): pg_cron fires an HTTP call through pg_net and forgets it. RunVouch tells you whether the Edge Function ran, finished and produced its result.
- [Render Cron Jobs](https://runvouch.com/integrations/render-cron): Wrap a Render cron job command with rv run to get MISSED, FAILED, NO_EVIDENCE and cost alerts, without adding a service.
- [Railway cron schedules](https://runvouch.com/integrations/railway-cron): Railway runs a service on a cron schedule and shows the logs. RunVouch adds the dead man's switch, evidence check and cost cap.
- [Fly.io scheduled Machines](https://runvouch.com/integrations/fly-io): Fly.io has no cron service; scheduled Machines and in-container cron both need an outside watchdog. rv run gives them one.
- [Cron inside Docker (supercronic, crond)](https://runvouch.com/integrations/docker-cron): Cron in a container dies with the container and logs to nowhere. Wrap each line with rv run so you learn about it before the next morning.
- [Apache Airflow](https://runvouch.com/integrations/airflow): Airflow alerts on task failure and SLA misses. RunVouch adds what a green DAG run cannot prove: the output exists, the run was on time, the LLM tasks stayed under budget.
- [Prefect](https://runvouch.com/integrations/prefect): Prefect marks runs Late when no worker picks them up. RunVouch pages you about it, checks the flow produced its result, and caps LLM spend per run.
- [Dagster](https://runvouch.com/integrations/dagster): Dagster schedules stop when the daemon stops. RunVouch alerts on the missing run, checks the asset was actually produced, and caps LLM cost per run.
- [Celery beat](https://runvouch.com/integrations/celery-beat): Celery beat schedules; workers execute. When either is gone, periodic tasks silently stop. RunVouch alerts on the missing run and on tasks that finish without their result.
- [APScheduler (in-process)](https://runvouch.com/integrations/apscheduler): In-process schedulers (APScheduler, node-cron, node-schedule) stop when the process stops. RunVouch notices from outside.
- [Temporal Schedules](https://runvouch.com/integrations/temporal): Temporal guarantees the workflow will eventually run. RunVouch tells you it did not run on time, and that it produced what it was supposed to.
- [Windmill](https://runvouch.com/integrations/windmill): Windmill schedules scripts and flows and shows their runs. RunVouch adds an outside dead man's switch, evidence and an LLM cost cap.
- [Make (Integromat)](https://runvouch.com/integrations/make): Make turns a scenario off after repeated errors and e-mails you once. RunVouch keeps watching: missed runs, empty runs, LLM cost per run.
- [Zapier](https://runvouch.com/integrations/zapier): Zapier pauses a Zap after too many errors and can hold tasks. RunVouch alerts when a scheduled Zap stops running or completes without doing the work.
- [Home Assistant automations](https://runvouch.com/integrations/home-assistant): Time-triggered Home Assistant automations that call scripts or LLM services can stop or no-op after an update. RunVouch notices from outside the house.
- [LangGraph](https://runvouch.com/integrations/langgraph): A LangGraph graph on a schedule can loop on a tool, overspend, or finish without its artifact. Wrap the run and report each tool call for retry-storm and cost detection.
- [CrewAI](https://runvouch.com/integrations/crewai): Wrap crew.kickoff() with RunVouch to cap cost per run, detect a crew looping on a tool and confirm the deliverable exists.
- [AutoGen](https://runvouch.com/integrations/autogen): Multi-agent chats in AutoGen can run to max_turns without producing the result. RunVouch caps the run, detects loops and checks the output.
- [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://runvouch.com/integrations/openai-agents-sdk): Wrap Runner.run() with RunVouch for a per-run cost cap, retry-storm detection on tool calls and a check that the agent produced its output.
- [Pydantic AI and smolagents](https://runvouch.com/integrations/pydantic-ai): Lightweight agent libraries have no scheduler and no budget. Wrapping the script with rv run gives a nightly Pydantic AI or smolagents job both.
- [Dify and Flowise](https://runvouch.com/integrations/dify-flowise): Dify and Flowise run workflows when something calls their API. Wrap the caller with rv run and report the run so a stopped scheduler or an empty answer gets an alert.
- [Ollama and local LLM batch jobs](https://runvouch.com/integrations/ollama-local-llm): Local models cost no API money, which is why nobody notices when the nightly job stalls on a swapped-out model or writes an empty file. rv run does.
- [n8n (community node)](https://runvouch.com/integrations/n8n): Install n8n-nodes-runvouch from Settings, Community Nodes. Start Run and End Run with evidence, or one Heartbeat node; alerts when the Schedule Trigger stops or the workflow runs and does nothing.
- [OpenClaw (verified-run skill)](https://runvouch.com/integrations/openclaw): Install the verified-run skill from integrations/openclaw. It wraps a scheduled OpenClaw task in a RunVouch run and reports the output file as evidence; missed, failed or empty runs alert you.

## Compare
- [vs Healthchecks.io](https://runvouch.com/vs/healthchecks): Ping monitor vs outcome watchdog.
- [vs Cronitor](https://runvouch.com/vs/cronitor): Ops monitoring vs agent monitoring.
- [vs Langfuse](https://runvouch.com/vs/langfuse): Tracing vs watchdog, complementary.
- [vs Dead Man's Snitch](https://runvouch.com/vs/dead-mans-snitch): Heartbeat vs heartbeat plus outcome.
- [vs Sentry Crons](https://runvouch.com/vs/sentry-crons): Exceptions vs silent failures.
- [vs Better Stack](https://runvouch.com/vs/better-stack): One vendor for uptime vs one job done well.
- [vs Uptime Kuma](https://runvouch.com/vs/uptime-kuma): Self-hosted push monitor vs agent watchdog.
- [vs Cronhub](https://runvouch.com/vs/cronhub): Cron monitor vs LLM job monitor.
- [vs Helicone](https://runvouch.com/vs/helicone): LLM proxy vs outside watchdog.
- [vs AgentOps](https://runvouch.com/vs/agentops): Session replay vs pager.
- [vs LangSmith](https://runvouch.com/vs/langsmith): Tracing vs the alert that there is something to trace.
